skill.name: An ending that lands
skill.why: The ending is what readers remember. Make it worth the trip.
skill.how: Solve the problem, show how the character has changed, or circle back to the start.

beats.say: Some endings just stop. Others land like a perfect jump.
'It was all a dream' cheats the reader. Skip it.
Land it by showing how the character changed.
beats.show: Tully, who never passed to anyone, **handed Mo the ball**.

beats.say: Or circle back to your very first line.
beats.show: Start: **The bin was growling.** End: **The bin was purring.**

beats.say: Or end on a picture that stays in your head.
beats.show: **The last firefly blinked once, then flew out to sea.**

weDo.frame: Wren's story starts: 'Mo's cooking had never won a single prize.'
weDo.hint: Which one links back to the first line?
weDo.success: It circles back to the prize, shows Mo finally won, and the gravy keeps it funny.

options.text: Mo held up the blue ribbon. It was covered in gravy, and he didn't care one bit.
Then Mo woke up, and it was all a dream.
options.reason: A dream ending cancels the whole story. The reader feels cheated.
It just stops. We never find out what happened to Mo or his cooking.

weDo.frame: Wren is sorting last lines from the crew's stories.
weDo.prompt: Put each ending in the right bin.
weDo.hint: Did the character earn this ending, or did it just happen?
weDo.success: Good endings solve the problem, show change or leave a picture. Dreams and random luck feel like cheating.

items.text: Wren opened the cage, and the owl lifted into the moonlight.
items.reason: We see the problem solved, with a picture to remember.

items.text: Suddenly a meteor hit, and everyone was fine.
items.reason: A random meteor comes out of nowhere. Nobody earned that ending.

items.text: Zed, who always quit, pressed play one more time.
items.reason: It shows Zed has changed by the end.

items.text: And then I woke up in my bed.
items.reason: A dream ending cancels everything that happened.

items.text: Anyway, that's all I can remember.
items.reason: It trails off instead of finishing the story.

creature.name: Swoopet
creature.blurb: An owl that circles the whole bay at night, then lands without a sound on the very branch it left from.

workshop.mentor: By the time we reached the jetty, the sky was turning pink and my torch had run flat. I didn't need it any more. Six months ago I wouldn't walk to the letterbox after dark. Now I'd spent a whole night in a cave full of bats, carrying a shoebox with one sleepy Creature inside. I knelt at the end of the jetty and lifted the lid. The little glow-worm blinked at me, then floated up and out over the water, a tiny green star heading home. I watched until I couldn't see it any more. Then I walked back up the hill, in the last of the dark, and I didn't hurry.
workshop.ask: Write the ending of a story. Ideas: Maxx is finally caught, the grand final siren, the ghost gets its wish, a lost dog comes home.
checklist: I showed how my character changed.
I finished with a picture or a callback.
I didn't use 'it was all a dream'.
